name: Proper Stable Sample Compression
definition: Let $\mathcal H\subseteq\{0,1\}^{X}$ be nonempty on a finite domain. A **proper reconstruction-stable unlabeled compression scheme of size $k$** consists of fixed maps $C$ and $\rho$: for every realizable partial labeled sample $s:S\to\{0,1\}$, the encoder selects an unordered key $C(s)\subseteq S$ of size at most $k$, and the decoder, given only that coordinate set, returns $\rho(C(s))\in\mathcal H$ consistent with $s$. No labels, original domain $S$, auxiliary messages, repetitions or ordering choices are transmitted. Stability requires $\rho(C(s|_T))=\rho(C(s))$ as functions on $X$ whenever $C(s)\subseteq T\subseteq S$; equality of the selected keys is not required. The **Proper Stable Sample Compression** $\mathrm{psUSC}(\mathcal H)$ is the least such $k$, or $+\infty$ if no scheme exists. Nonexistence can occur even for finite classes, for the balanced six-split class.
graph_summary: Fewest retained coordinates, with no labels or messages, for proper reconstruction unchanged by deletion of unretained examples; $+\infty$ if no such scheme exists.
origin_references: The stability condition for sample compression schemes is used in \cite{bousquet2020proper,hanneke2021stable}.

p_monotonic.proof: For a projected-realizable sample, apply the original proper stable scheme while viewing the sample on the retained coordinates as a sample on the original domain, then restrict the reconstructed member of $\mathcal H$.  It lies in the projected class, stays consistent, and has the same stability and compression size.

comments: Conditioning monotonicity is unverified. The former append-compress-erase argument did not supply a well-defined decoder after distinct keys lose their fixed coordinates. An explicit collision disproves that construction for an ordinary proper encoder, not monotonicity of the parameter. The stable case requires a separate collision argument. See sync/COMPRESSION_CONDITIONING_AUDIT.md in the source repository (September 20, 2026).
